title: Kanda Poha
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.
description: Flattened rice (poha) tempered with mustard, curry leaves, turmeric, onions, peanuts and a squeeze of lemon. A light, everyday Maharashtrian breakfast staple, especially popular in Mumbai and Pune.
steps: Rinse poha gently and drain; let it soften.
Temper mustard seeds, curry leaves, green chillies in oil.
Add onions and sauté until translucent; add turmeric and peanuts.
Add poha, salt and a pinch of sugar; mix gently.
Finish with lemon juice and fresh coriander.
tips: Do not over-soak poha or it turns mushy.
Dadpe pohe is a no-cook variation with grated coconut.

title: Misal Pav
jainNotes: Contains onion, garlic, and ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.
description: Spicy sprouted-lentil curry (usal) topped with farsan, onion, coriander and lemon, served with soft pav. Kolhapuri and Puneri styles are especially famous for their heat and depth.
ingredients: 1 cup sprouted matki or mixed sprouts
Misal or Kolhapuri masala, turmeric, chilli powder
steps: Cook sprouts with spices and water to make a spicy usal/rassa.
Prepare a dry potato or sprout topping if desired.
Assemble in a bowl: usal, toppings, farsan, onion, coriander.
Serve immediately with buttered pav and lemon wedges.
tips: Kolhapuri misal is famously fiery; Puneri is slightly milder and tangier.

title: Thalipeeth
jainNotes: Contains onion - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion.
description: Savoury multi-grain flatbread made from bhajani (roasted grain and pulse flour mix), onions, spices and coriander. Pressed by hand and cooked on a tawa; typically eaten with yogurt or thecha.
ingredients: 2 cups bhajani flour (or mix of jowar, bajra, rice, besan, wheat)
steps: Mix flours with chopped onion, spices and salt.
Knead into a soft dough with water.
Pat into thick rounds on a greased plastic sheet or banana leaf.
Transfer to hot tawa and cook on both sides with a little oil until crisp.
tips: Farali (fasting) version uses sabudana, potato and singhada flour.

title: Sabudana Khichdi
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, use sweet potato as substitute or omit potato.
description: Soaked sago pearls tempered with cumin, green chillies, peanuts and boiled potato. A classic fasting (farali) dish that is naturally free of onion and garlic when prepared traditionally.
ingredients: Cumin seeds, green chillies, curry leaves (optional)
steps: Soak sabudana until soft but not mushy; drain well.
Temper cumin and chillies in ghee or oil.
Add potato and peanuts, then sabudana.
Cook on low heat, stirring gently, until translucent.
Finish with lemon and coriander.
tips: Perfect for Ekadashi and other fasting days.

title: Varan Bhaat
jainNotes: Ingredients are Jain-compatible (toor dal, ghee, cumin, hing, rice). No onion, garlic, or root vegetables. Ensure hing is Jain-certified.
description: Simple, comforting toor dal (varan) tempered with ghee, cumin and hing, poured over steamed rice. The everyday heart of a Maharashtrian vegetarian meal, often finished with a spoon of pure ghee.
steps: Pressure-cook dal with turmeric and water until soft.
Mash lightly and adjust consistency.
Temper ghee with cumin and hing; pour over dal.
Serve hot over plain rice with a dollop of ghee.
tips: Often paired with a dry vegetable (suki bhaji) and koshimbir.

title: Pithla Bhakri (Zunka Bhakri)
jainNotes: Contains onion and garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit onion-garlic.
description: Rustic chickpea-flour gravy (pithla/zunka) cooked with onions, green chillies and spices, served with thick jowar or bajra bhakri. Quintessential rural Maharashtrian comfort food.
ingredients: Jowar or bajra flour for bhakri
steps: Make a thin batter of besan with water and spices.
Temper mustard and onions; pour in batter and cook, stirring until thickened.
Knead millet flour with water, pat into thick bhakris and cook on tawa or open flame.
Serve pithla with hot bhakri and thecha.
tips: Zunka is the drier version; pithla is slightly more gravy-like.

title: Bharli Vangi
jainNotes: Contains onion, garlic, and tamarind/kokum. No root vegetables besides brinjal. Onion-garlic are not consumed by Jains.
description: Small brinjals stuffed with a spiced peanut-coconut-goda masala mixture and cooked until soft. A classic festive and everyday vegetable dish of Maharashtra.
ingredients: Roasted peanuts, grated coconut, goda masala
Onion, garlic, sesame, chilli powder, tamarind or kokum
steps: Slit brinjals carefully, keeping stems intact.
Prepare stuffing of ground peanuts, coconut and spices.
Stuff the brinjals and cook in a little oil with remaining masala and water until tender.
tips: Goda masala is the signature sweet-savoury spice blend of Maharashtra.

title: Kolhapuri Tambda Rassa / Mutton
jainNotes: Contains mutton, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
description: Fiery Kolhapuri-style mutton in a rich red (tambda) gravy made with a special dry coconut-chilli spice mix. Often served with pandhra (white) rassa and bhakri or rice.
ingredients: Kolhapuri masala or dry coconut + red chilli paste
steps: Marinate and pressure-cook mutton until tender.
Prepare a spicy onion-coconut-chilli gravy.
Combine and simmer until the oil separates and flavours intensify.
Serve with bhakri, rice or pav.
tips: Authentic versions are extremely spicy; adjust heat to taste.

title: Puran Poli
jainNotes: Contains chana dal (allowed for Jains), but preparation may involve ghee and hing. Ensure hing is Jain-certified. No onion, garlic, or root vegetables.
description: Soft whole-wheat flatbread stuffed with a sweet filling of cooked chana dal, jaggery and cardamom. A festive favourite prepared for Gudi Padwa, Holi and Ganesh Chaturthi.
steps: Cook chana dal until soft; mash and cook with jaggery into a thick puran.
Knead soft dough with flour and ghee.
Stuff portions of dough with puran, seal and roll gently.
Cook on tawa with ghee until golden spots appear on both sides.
tips: Serve warm with pure ghee or katachi amti (the leftover dal water).

title: Saoji Mutton
jainNotes: Contains mutton, onion, garlic - not consumed by Jains.
description: Spicy Vidarbha-style mutton curry from the Saoji community of Nagpur, known for its complex dry-spice blend and rich, oily gravy. Typically eaten with bhakri or rice.
ingredients: Saoji masala (or homemade mix of dry coconut, red chillies, poppy, sesame, whole spices)
steps: Marinate mutton with spices.
Fry onions and prepare the strong spice paste.
Cook mutton in the masala until tender and oil floats on top.
tips: Distinct from Kolhapuri; more complex and aromatic.

title: Vada Pav
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) and garlic - not consumed by Jains.
description: Mumbai's iconic street food — a deep-fried spiced potato dumpling (batata vada) sandwiched in a soft pav with dry garlic chutney, green chutney and fried green chilli.
ingredients: Boiled potatoes, green chillies, garlic, mustard, turmeric
Dry garlic-red chilli chutney, green chutney
steps: Mash potatoes with tempered spices and form balls.
Dip in thick besan batter and deep-fry until golden.
Slit pav, spread chutneys, insert vada and serve with fried chilli.
tips: Best eaten hot from a street stall; originated in Mumbai in the 1960s.

title: Pav Bhaji
jainNotes: Contains potato (root vegetable) and onion - not consumed by Jains.
description: Mashed mixed-vegetable curry cooked with pav-bhaji masala and plenty of butter, served with toasted pav, onion and lemon. A beloved Mumbai street-food classic.
steps: Boil and mash vegetables.
Sauté onion-tomato base with pav-bhaji masala and butter.
Add mashed vegetables and simmer, mashing further.
Toast pav in butter and serve with bhaji, raw onion and lemon.
tips: Generous butter is traditional and essential for authentic flavour.

title: Kothimbir Vadi
jainNotes: Contains ginger - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit ginger.
description: Steamed and then shallow- or deep-fried squares of besan, fresh coriander, sesame and spices. A popular tea-time snack across Maharashtra.
ingredients: Sesame seeds, green chillies, ginger, turmeric, chilli powder
steps: Mix besan with coriander and spices into a thick batter.
Steam in a greased tray until firm.
Cool, cut into squares or diamonds.
Shallow-fry or deep-fry until crisp.
tips: Can also be baked for a lighter version.

title: Sol Kadhi
jainNotes: Contains garlic - not consumed by Jains. For Jain version, omit garlic.
description: Refreshing Konkani drink-cum-digestive made from kokum extract and coconut milk, tempered lightly and served chilled. Often accompanies seafood meals or stands alone as a cooling snack.
steps: Soak kokum in warm water and extract the sour liquid.
Mix with coconut milk and salt.
Temper lightly if desired and chill.
Serve cold, garnished with coriander.
tips: Excellent digestive after a heavy meal.
